To fix (3)

To fix Exact P-Values

What we found

We found 4 imprecise p values out of 41 detected p values.

Show details

Reporting p values imprecisely (e.g., p < .05) reduces transparency, reproducibility, and re-use (e.g., in p value meta-analyses). Best practice is to report exact p-values with three decimal places (e.g., p = .032) unless p values are smaller than 0.001, in which case you can use p < .001.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., “decreased at the p < .05 significance threshold”).

P-Value Text
ps ≤ .008 The dissident correlation exceeded the dangerous correlation in all samples (Williams’s ts ≥ 8.65, ps < .001) and the derogated correlation in Studies 2, 5, and 6 (ts = 6.67, 5.76, and 2.68, ps ≤ .008), but not in Study 4 (t = 0.11, p = .911).
ps ≤ .003 In simultaneous multiple regressions (Table 3), RWA was independently associated with more negative attitudes toward environmentalists in Studies 2, 4, and 6 (βs = .19 to .31, ps < .001) and marginally in Study 5 (β = .16, p = .053); SDO did so in all four samples (βs = .13 to .48, ps ≤ .003).
ps < .002 Environmentalists loaded most strongly on the dissident factor (standardized λs = .51 to .57 across samples), weakly on the derogated factor (.10 to .12), and negatively on the dangerous factor (-.15 to -.11; all ps < .002).
ps ≤ .021 Conversely, SDO emerged as the stronger predictor of derogated prejudice, with significantly stronger paths than RWA in Studies 4, 5, and 6 (Δβ = .23 to .48, Holm ps ≤ .021).

The APA manual states: Report exact p values (e.g., p = .031) to two or three decimal places. However, report p values less than .001 as p < .001. However, 2 decimals is too imprecise for many use-cases (e.g., a p value meta-analysis), so report p values with three digits.

American Psychological Association (2020). Publication manual of the American Psychological Association, 7 edition. American Psychological Association.

To check (4)

To check Non-Significant P Value Check

What we found

We found 5 non-significant p values that should be checked for appropriate interpretation.

Show details

Meta-scientific research has shown nonsignificant p values are commonly misinterpreted. It is incorrect to infer that there is ‘no effect’, ‘no difference’, or that groups are ‘the same’ after p > 0.05.

It is possible that there is a true non-zero effect, but that the study did not detect it. Make sure your inference acknowledges that it is possible that there is a non-zero effect. It is correct to include the effect is ‘not significantly’ different, although this just restates that p > 0.05.

Metacheck does not yet analyze automatically whether sentences which include non-significant p-values are correct, but we recommend manually checking the sentences below for possible misinterpreted non-significant p values.

Text Sentence

p = .520 Restricting environmentalists to the dangerous or derogated factor substantially worsened fit (Δχ²(2) ≥ 79.1), whereas restricting it to the dissident factor did not worsen fit in Study 2 (Δχ²(2) = 1.3, p = .520) and produced the smallest loss elsewhere (Δχ²(2) = 11.7 to 72.2).

p = .287 The same differential pattern was observed in Study 2, although the difference did not reach significance (Δβ = .17, p = .287).

Q66_10 yes CWB10)Honestidade é sempre a melhor opção. Q66_10 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_11 yes CWB11)É sempre importante conceder o benefício da dúvida aos outros. A maioria das pessoas é confiável se você acreditar nelas. Q66_11 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_12 yes DWB1)Meu conhecimento e minha experiência me dizem que a sociedade é um lugar seguro e estável, em que a maioria das pessoas é fundamentalmente boa. Q66_12 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_13 yes DWB2)Embora pareça que as coisas estão ficando mais perigosas e caóticas, isso não é verdade. Todos os momentos históricos têm seus problemas, e as chances de ter uma vida segura nunca foram tão altas quanto agora. Q66_13 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_14 yes DWB3)O ‘’fim’’ não está próximo. Pessoas que pensam que terremotos, guerras e fome significam que Deus pode estar prestes a destruir o mundo estão sendo tolas. Q66_14 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_15 yes DWB4)Apesar do que se ouve sobre a criminalidade nas ruas, provavelmente nada mudou, a frequência desses crimes é a mesma de antes. Q66_15 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_16 yes DWB5)Nós não vivemos em um mundo perigoso. Se as pessoas tomam algumas precauções, provavelmente nada de ruim acontecerá a elas. Q66_16 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_17 yes DWB6)Parece que a cada ano há menos pessoas verdadeiramente decentes e mais pessoas imorais, que ameaçam todos os outros. Q66_17 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_18 yes DWB7)Tudo indica que o caos e a anarquia podem emergir a qualquer momento. Todos os sinais estão apontando para isso. Q66_18 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_19 yes DWB8)Há muitas pessoas perigosas na sociedade, que podem atacar as outras por pura maldade, sem motivo nenhum. Q66_19 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_2 yes CWB2)Não existe isso de “certo” e “errado”. No fim, o que importa é o que se pode ganhar com isso. Q66_2 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_20 yes DWB9)Meu conhecimento e minha experiência me dizem que a sociedade em que nós vivemos é um lugar perigoso e imprevisível. Q66_20 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_21 yes DWB10)Os valores e modos de vida das pessoas de bem estão sendo ameaçados e perturbados por pessoas más. Q66_21 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_22 yes DWB11)A cada dia, conforme a sociedade vai se tornando mais sem lei e selvagem, as chances de uma pessoa ser roubada, agredida ou assassinada só aumentam. Q66_22 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_3 yes CWB3)Uma das habilidades mais úteis que uma pessoa deveria desenvolver é olhar alguém nos olhos e mentir de maneira convincente. Q66_3 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_4 yes CWB4)Meu conhecimento e minha experiência me dizem que o mundo em que vivemos é basicamente uma selva competitiva, em que os mais adaptados sobrevivem e obtêm sucesso. Q66_4 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_5 yes CWB5)Poder, riqueza e sucesso são tudo que importa, afinal, aqueles que têm poder fazem o que quiserem. Q66_5 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_6 yes CWB6)Basicamente, as pessoas são objetos a serem friamente manipulados para se obter benefícios pessoais. Q66_6 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_7 yes CWB7)A vida não é determinada pela “lei do mais forte”. Devemos deixar a compaixão e a ética serem nossos guias. Q66_7 Study6Dataset.sav labelled
Q66_8 yes CWB8)É melhor ser amado do que ser temido. Q66_8 Study6Dataset.sav labelled

Absolute Paths

Best programming practice is to use relative file paths (e.g., ‘./files’) instead of absolute file paths (e.g., ‘C://Lakens/project_dir/files’) as these folder names do not exist on other computers. No absolute file paths were found in any of the code files.

Working Directory (setwd)

Best programming practice is to avoid setwd() in analysis code: it hardcodes an assumption about the working directory (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine), so the code breaks when run anywhere else. Keep the working directory as the caller sets it and use relative paths. No setwd() calls were found in any of the code files.

Package Installation (install.packages)

Best programming practice is to avoid install.packages() in analysis code: it installs software on whoever runs the script without asking, which is at minimum disruptive (an unexpected install, network access, a package version the author never tested against) and at worst a security risk if it points at an untrusted repository. Document required packages instead (a README, or a list of them: an renv.lock/DESCRIPTION for R, a requirements.txt for Python). No install.packages() calls were found in any of the code files.

Libraries / Imports

Best programming practice is to load all required libraries/imports in one block near the top of the code. In all code files, libraries/imports were loaded in one block.

Packages / Dependencies

Power Analysis Check

No power analyses were detected.

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen’s d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.
